data.title: The ranked bots have ordinary player names
data.tldr: The game has said since March 2025 that some ranks use AI opponents. In the code there are 36 of them, with names like Alex, Andy, Drew, Cathy and Vickie, levels 6–15, real icons and greetings. Bot games run on your phone.
data.player_impact: That 'player' who never emotes may be a bot, especially at low ranks. The server also tracks a hidden ranked losing streak that may decide when you get one.

data.title: Since B1a, the CPU opponent plays the same move every time
data.tldr: Solo battle AI used to sample moves with randomness (temperature 3.0). From the B1a release (Dec 17 2025), every difficulty runs at temperature 0, always taking its top-rated move.
data.player_impact: Given the same board, the CPU now makes the same choice, so its habits are learnable. If a line beats an Expert deck once, the CPU's side of it should repeat. Your draws and coin flips still vary.

data.title: Wonder Pick events quietly cut your Chansey and Bonus pick odds
data.tldr: The usual rolls are known: each time your Wonder Pick list refreshes there's a 2.5% chance of a Chansey pick and 20% of a free Bonus pick. Since May 2026, during Wonder Pick events, those drop to 1.3% and 5%.
data.player_impact: Hunting Chansey or Bonus picks? Do it outside Wonder Pick events.

data.title: Your very first tutorial pack choice permanently set your Flair route
data.tldr: Which of the three tutorial packs you picked assigned you route A, B or C. Each route sees about 5,400 route-only Flair options for the same cards. It can't be changed.
data.player_impact: Your friends may see different Flair for the same card in the exchange shop. That's your tutorial pick, not a bug.

data.title: Tapping the coin does nothing: the flip is decided before you touch it
data.tldr: The 'tap to flip' action carries no data. The battle engine has already decided the result: on the server in PvP, on your phone from a secure random seed in solo play.
data.player_impact: There's no timing trick for coin flips. Tap whenever you like.

data.title: The CPU is handed your whole deck, then blindfolded
data.tldr: The solo CPU's code builds a list of every card in your deck, hidden ones included. But its neural network masks out any card it hasn't seen or worked out, so only your revealed cards affect its moves.
data.player_impact: Your tech card can still surprise it. We changed hidden cards in the real model and its decisions didn't move at all.

data.title: Deluxe packs quietly favour the regular print over the foil print
data.tldr: In Deluxe packs' slot-3 ◆◆◆ label, regular prints are weighted about 3.5–3.8× more than parallel-foil prints. These are the only non-uniform card weights in the game.
data.player_impact: If you're chasing the foil version of a Deluxe ◆◆◆ card, expect it to take roughly 3.5× longer than the regular one.

data.title: In current Wonder Pick you pay when the cards flip, not when you pick
data.tldr: Since the V2 flow, stamina, revival clocks and PokéGold are all spent in the 'Snoop' step. The final pick request carries no cost at all.
data.player_impact: Once the cards flip face-down, you've already paid. Closing the app there doesn't refund you, and only one Wonder Pick can be in progress at a time.

data.title: Trades keep a card's Flair and gold frame; gifts strip them
data.tldr: A traded card carries its Flair skin and frame. A card given through Give Card sends only the card, language and expansion.
data.player_impact: Want a friend to get your shiny Flair copy? Trade it. Gifting sends a plain copy.

data.title: The game logs HOW you open packs, including the pinch-open
data.tldr: Analytics events record whether you opened a pack the normal swipe way, from the back, or with the 'PotatoBag' pinch gesture. They also record every home-screen tap, favourites and full-screen card views.
data.player_impact: Your play style is measured in fine detail. The pinch-open gesture's internal name is 'PotatoBag', as in tearing open a bag of chips.
